key_insight: eMOOD replaces MOOD’s traditional troubled-cell test with entropy production to detect non-smooth regions more selectively and efficiently on unstructured meshes.
engineering_relevance: This improves shock-capturing finite-volume simulations by reducing unnecessary cell flagging, lowering memory overhead, and speeding up high-order compressible-flow solvers without sacrificing robustness.
method: Uses numerical entropy generation as a compact troubled-cell indicator instead of a relaxed discrete maximum principle.
Integrates the detector into both a classical MOOD cascade and a MOOD-CWENO hybrid scheme.
Implemented in UCNS3D for parallel high-order finite-volume simulations on unstructured meshes.
evidence_signal: Across benchmarks including Shu-Osher, double Mach reflection, forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble interaction, and triple material point problems, eMOOD reportedly flags up to 75% fewer cells and delivers up to 20% speed-up while maintaining solution quality.
watch_item: Entropy-based detection is physically motivated but may need careful calibration to remain reliable across very different flow regimes, meshes, and solver settings.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
